title: Batching edge-case sync + KV cache gap triage (Apr 11 2027)
content:
Meeting purpose:
- Quick sync on strange tail-latency spikes observed last week when coalescer + kernel prefetch paths interact with KV cache eviction. Triage notes, hypotheses, experiments, and immediate mitigation steps.

Attendees:
- Lena Ortiz (notes)
- Marco Chen
- Priya Nair
- Evan Morales
- Sachin Rao
- Guests: support-engineer Jon Park (observability context)

Context / symptom summary (what we saw)
- Starting Thu Apr 8, several customer traces show intermittent p99 token generation latency jumping from ~210ms -> ~1.2s in hosted region us-west-2 for short bursts (~5-10m).
- The bursts correlate with moderate throughput (250-500 qps) for sequences ~800-1200 tokens.
- Affected model family: community/opt-13b variants (quantized).
- Alerts triggered: tail-latency SLO breach (alert INF-TL-7) and concurrent errors increased by ~0.2%.
- Initial triage suggests coalescer groups were building batches but some microbatches stayed stalled waiting for KV prefill; an eviction wave removed root prefixes causing recompute.

Important observations from traces / metrics (Jon):
- Timeline: most spikes start within 30s after a scheduled cache-trimmer job (kv-trimmer-v2) runs.
- KV cache hit-rate dips ~18% during spikes.
- Kernel-level logs show repeated prefetch attempts for the same KV segment (hot-prefix thrash) with exponential backoff (~120ms between attempts).
- When prefetch fails, coalescer logic falls back to synchronous generation but still expects cached KV and ends up executing extra attention passes -> double work.

Hypotheses (ranked)
1) kv-trimmer job is too aggressive for long-seq workloads and evicts prefixes that are still being prefetched by in-flight requests; this causes repeated re-prefetch and kernel stalls.
2) Kernel prefetch path has a small race where a prefetch-in-flight flag isn't observed by the coalescer, so multiple microbatches issue redundant prefetches, thereby saturating the device IO path.
3) Coalescer waiting logic has a starvation window: when a microbatch misses its prefill it will wait up to X ms for a KV but, due to scheduling jitter, the next tick groups additional requests and extends queuing leading to amplified latency.
4) Edge-case in quantized kernel path increases prefetch cost for certain shard alignments leading to longer prefetch durations (seen in opt-13b q4_0 path).

Experiments run over Apr 9-11 (Marco / Priya)
- Exp A (Apr 9): Disable kv-trimmer-v2 for a 4-hour window on a canary host-pool serving the same traffic pattern. Result: p99 stabilized to baseline; KV hit-rate stayed higher.
- Exp B (Apr 10): Introduce lightweight prefetch backpressure: allow only 2 concurrent prefetches per device per prefix. Result: p99 reduced by ~220ms during peak; throughput unchanged. CPU overhead + slight increase in tail for unrelated small requests.
- Exp C (Apr 11): Tweak coalescer wait-time from 45ms -> 25ms and add a fast-fail path if prefetch not started within 10ms. Result: reduced amplification but increased number of duplicated compute runs (small).
- Observed side-effects: disabling trimmer increased memory pressure on hosts by ~6%, but OOMs not observed. Backpressure reduced redundant kernel prefetch bursts.

Decisions taken in meeting
- Short-term rollback: re-enable trimmer but with a soft TTL extension for prefixes touched in last 60s (to be implemented as kv-trimmer-v2 soft-grace). Owner: Sachin. ETA: Apr 13.
- Medium-term: Implement per-prefix prefetch semaphore to bound concurrent prefetch attempts from coalescer across microbatches (limit default 3). Owner: Marco + Evan. RFC/PR targeted by Apr 20 (PR:1284 is the initial draft).
- Coalescer change: reduce max wait window and add observability metric for 'prefetch_wait_start' and 'prefetch_wait_end' to measure stomping. Owner: Priya. ETA: Apr 18.
- Kernel team to review quantized prefetch path for shard-alignment worst-case (~opt-13b q4_0). Owner: Evan. ETA: Apr 22.

Action items (clear owners & dates)
- Sachin: implement soft-grace TTL for trimmer (kv-trimmer-v2). Deploy to canary and monitor for 24h. Due: 2027-04-13.
- Marco/Evan: finalize per-prefix prefetch semaphore and benchmark on local perf cluster (tools/perf-cluster). Create PR and benchmark doc. Due: 2027-04-20.
- Priya: coalescer wait-time tuning + new observability spans; add to tracing and create dashboard tile. Due: 2027-04-18.
- Lena: collect 10 representative traces (p99 samples) and assemble a short slide with waterfall and kernel logs for infra review. Due: 2027-04-14.
- Jon (support): add a temporary alert that watches for "KV hit-rate drop > 10% coincident with p99 > 800ms" so we can detect recurrence. Due: 2027-04-12 (today).
- Evan: kernel prefetch microbench for q4_0 alignment (profiling script + flamegraphs). Due: 2027-04-22.

Notes from code review / patch ideas (Marco)
- Add atomic 'prefetch_owner' token per prefix in device memory to avoid repeated prefetches when a prefetch is already in-flight (small device memory cost but cuts redundant IO).
- Provide a 'fast-path' response for coalescer when prefetch is known-to-be-stale (return small dummy response so caller can reissue with fresh prefix) — this is disruptive, prefer semaphore approach first.
- Consider adding prefetch batching: if 3 microbatches all need same prefix, issue one aggregated prefetch request (kernel-level aggregation). More complex, medium-term.

Risk assessment
- Soft-grace TTL: low risk (server-side only; ups memory pressure). Keep canary hours and monitor.
- Prefetch semaphore: medium risk (possible underutilization if limit too low). We'll tune per-device.
- Coalescer wait tuning: low risk but may increase duplicate compute cost; accept small cost to avoid 1s tail spikes.
- Kernel changes: higher risk (C++/CUDA surfaces). Need careful perf/regression testing on perf-cluster and QA.

Observability additions (Priya / Jon)
- New metrics/spans to add: prefetch_attempts_per_prefix, prefetch_concurrency_per_device, coalescer_wait_ms, kv_prefetch_failures, kv_hit_rate_by_prefix_age.
- Dashboard: add "prefetch pressure" panel to existing serving-runtime per-pool dashboard.
- Tracing: annotate spans with prefix_id, prefetch_owner_token, prefetch_latency_ms.

Follow-ups / discussion items (open questions)
- What TTL grace values balance memory vs stability? (Sachin to propose 30s/60s/120s tests).
- Are there other trimmer jobs (older versions) that could overlap? Need full inventory. Owner: Lena. Due: Apr 15.
- Can we simulate hot-prefix storms in perf-cluster? Need workload generator that mimics long-seq tail traffic. Owner: Marco. Due: Apr 19.

Meeting takeaways
- Root cause likely interplay of aggressive trimming + unbounded prefetch bursts; coalescer waiting amplifies the effect leading to 1s p99 spikes.
- Immediate mitigations (soft-grace TTL + prefetch backpressure) already show positive results on canary.
- Kernel-level hardening needed but is medium-term.

Appendix: quick command snippets and links used in triage
- jq pipeline to extract slow request traces: 
  gzcat traces-2027-04-08-*.jsonl.gz | jq 'select(.latency_ms > 800) | {req_id: .id, trace: .trace}' > p99-samples.json
- perf-cluster run command (local): 
  ./perf/run_workload --model opt-13b-q4_0 --seq-len 1024 --qps 400 --duration 600s --pattern hot-prefix-storm
- Kernel debug log filter: 
  grep "prefetch" /var/log/kernel-prefetch.log | tail -n 200

Raw snippets from trace (anonymized)
- "prefetch_start prefix=0x7fa3ed3c attempts=1 device=0"
- "coalescer_wait start=161905230 ms=47 prefix=0x7fa3ed3c owner=null"
- "prefetch_fail prefix=0x7fa3ed3c reason=evicted_during_prefetch"

If you have questions or want to take ownership of an item, ping in #serving-runtime with the action id and I'll add you to the tracker.

Next sync: Mon Apr 18, 10:30am PT — short standup to check canary metrics and perf numbers.
